headline: Jensen Huang Is Back, and So Is His Plaque at Denny’s

paragraphs.text: America’s diner is always open, especially for Jensen Huang.
Denny’s, the restaurant chain, has reaffirmed its ties to Mr. Huang, the co-founder of Nvidia, days after he was reinstated as the company’s chief executive.

“Every story starts somewhere. We’re proud to be part of Jensen’s,” Denny’s posted on its social media accounts on Wednesday, alluding to Mr. Huang’s path from washing dishes at a Denny’s as a teenager to becoming one of the most powerful figures in artificial intelligence and one of the world’s richest people.

Legend has it that Mr. Huang developed the idea for Nvidia in a booth at a Denny’s in San Jose, Calif., in 1993 with his co-founders Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. In 2023, the restaurant put a plaque above that booth commemorating Nvidia’s beginnings, inviting Mr. Huang to unveil it.

Two weeks ago, Mr. Huang resigned as chief executive of the chip maker after revelations that he’d had extramarital affairs with an executive who reported to him and with a woman whom U.S. officials had identified as a Chinese spy.
The day after his resignation, Denny’s wrote in its post on Wednesday, the company learned that the commemorative plaque had come down.
“We put the plaque right back up where it belongs,” it said.

Denny’s did not say when the plaque was restored — and multiple calls to the San Jose location on Thursday morning went unanswered — but its statement came two days after Nvidia’s board of directors reinstalled Mr. Huang following pressure from President Trump.

Mr. Huang’s comeback has been met with mixed reactions. Some congressional Republicans have harshly criticized Nvidia’s decision to reinstate him and argued that the Trump administration had not provided adequate assurances that it had resolved national security concerns surrounding the company. Mr. Huang’s allies, including in the tech sector, have supported him, with Elon Musk comparing his exit to “kicking Michael Jordan off your team.”
Denny’s, too, offered its unequivocal support for Mr. Huang. “We couldn’t be prouder of the history we share,” it wrote.
The company’s statement was met with bafflement on X, where one user said it “might actually be one of the cringiest things I’ve ever seen on this website.”

If such allegiance to another company’s executive seems out of the ordinary, Mr. Huang is no ordinary executive. Having co-founded Nvidia at 30, he built it into a company worth $5.8 trillion at its peak.
But even as he cultivated a rock star persona in the tech world, leather jackets and all, Mr. Huang often evoked his humble beginnings at Denny’s.

He has said that at 15, he got his first job at a Denny’s in Oregon, where his family lived after immigrating from Taiwan. On Thursday, his LinkedIn profile listed two jobs: founder and chief executive of Nvidia (1993-present) and “dishwasher, busboy, waiter” at Denny’s (1978-1983).
“I was a dishwasher, I was a busboy, I waited tables,” Mr. Huang said, according to a Nvidia blog post in 2023 about the unveiling of the plaque. “No one can carry more coffee cups than I can.”

Denny’s has hundreds of locations across the United States, including eight in San Jose, Calif., in the heart of Silicon Valley. The chain’s slogan, “America’s diner is always open,” is meant literally — Denny’s really is open all day, every day, Thanksgiving and Christmas included — but also as a way to showcase the chain’s philosophy.
“We’re open to whomever you are, and we greet customers with open arms and have an open mind,” Peter McGuinness, the chief executive of the agency behind the slogan, told The New York Times in 2011.
For a corporate titan looking to shake off sex scandals and the whiff of espionage, that is a welcome message.
